pr_body:
This adds a way to log current threads in plain text to logs. This way we do not need to decode them and can search by stack trace in logs (for example to know if the issue is recurring). Please note, this produces a multi-line log entry.



Closes: #110915
pr_title: Add a way to log hot threads in plain text

review_comment:
This avoids sleep after collecting the last sample.
Should make collection much faster when executing with `threadElementsSnapshotCount=1`
Good idea! Wrapping the sleep inside a `if (j < threadElementsSnapshotCount - 1)` check might be a smaller changeset.
nit: maybe instead adding an if in the for loop is a bit more readable.
I prefer to make a loop one iteration shorter rather than every time check if it is the last iteration.
This slows the tests down doesn't it? Previously we were not actually sleeping here at all, whereas now we do. Is this change needed for this utility?

I think it'd help to include some more metadata in the log message rather than just formatting it all as plain text like this - i.e. using `org.elasticsearch.common.logging.ESLogMessage`. For instance could we break out the thread name, the name of the containing pool and the prefix string?

This is technically possible but would require much bigger refactoring to introduce domain model for the stack trace, thread name, cpu usage as well as various output modes (such as MEM). I would like to leave it outside of the scope of this change.

I wonder whether it is worthwhile to add similar counting and summary of total number of threads similar to how hot-threads are logged. We don't really need the counting to preserve orders for decompressing, but it seems useful to have a summary on how many threads are logged?
++ it'd be useful to check we hadn't missed any log messages.

We synced offline and agreed that search with prefix (likely unqiue) should be able to get us all the relevant entries without counting and summary. They might still be useful if somehow ingestion had problem to take in all data. But that should be a rare case and we can have follow-ups if we really need them.
what was the specific use case that would benefit from this? Maybe we could use it there with this PR too? otherwise this seems unused.

Correct, it is currently unused. The goal of the pr is to introduce the mechanism to log hot threads in plain threads without changing existing behavior. Existing `logLocalHotThreads` usages could be moved to `logLocalCurrentThreads` eventually. Meanwhile this change could help with serverless performance investigations.
